environment: macOS (Darwin 25.6), git 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155), python3 via cli-runner and pycall, node --test

cases.title: Unicode whitespace and control characters in the format raise Fail, never another exception
cases.given: The unicode-whitespace and control-chars corpus families, each put into a/<value>/{name}, plus tab, newline, U+00A0 and U+3000 forms.
cases.when: validate_format runs on each format through pycall.
cases.then: Each format that holds Python whitespace, or whose sample name git refuses, raises Fail. No format raises another exception.
cases.expected: Fail for every whitespace or git-refused format; no other exception.
cases.actual: All whitespace and C0 control forms raise Fail. Six corpus entries return the format: U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF, U+180E and C1 U+009B. Python \s does not match them, and git accepts them.
cases.specSource: R-017 quote: no whitespace, and the sample passes git check-ref-format --branch

evidence.title: accepted corpus entries
evidence.inline:
unicode-whitespace zwsp 'a\u200bb' -> return
unicode-whitespace zwnj 'a\u200cb' -> return
unicode-whitespace zwj 'a\u200db' -> return
unicode-whitespace bom '\ufeffa' -> return
unicode-whitespace mongolian-vs 'a\u180eb' -> return
control-chars c1-csi '\x9b31m' -> return
all other entries -> Fail

cases.title: Zero-width characters get the same verdict as git
cases.given: The formats a\u200b/{name}, a\ufeff/{name}, \u200b{name}, a/{name}\u200d and a\u2060/{name}.
cases.when: validate_format runs on each, and git check-ref-format --branch runs on the same sample name.
cases.then: validate_format accepts exactly when git accepts, and returns the input unchanged.
cases.actual: All five return the input; git accepts all five sample names.
cases.specSource: R-017 quote: name(fmt, "slice", id="S-001") passes git check-ref-format --branch

cases.title: Git-refused literal parts raise Fail with git's reason
cases.given: 23 formats: .., .lock, leading dash forms, --upload-pack=, leading or trailing slash, //, ~ ^ : ? * [ \, /.b, leading dot, trailing dot, \x01, DEL, ESC.
cases.when: validate_format runs on each; git check-ref-format --branch runs on each sample name.
cases.then: git refuses every sample, and validate_format raises Fail with check-ref-format and is not a valid branch name in the message.
cases.expected: Fail with git's reason for all 23.
cases.actual: Fail with git's reason for all 23.
cases.specSource: R-017 acceptance: the invalid-ref rejection carries git check-ref-format's reason

evidence.title: sample messages
evidence.inline:
'sdlc/{name}..' -> Fail: ... gives 'sdlc/S-001..', which git check-ref-format refuses: fatal: 'sdlc/S-001..' is not a valid branch name
'a\x01/{name}' -> Fail: ... fatal: 'a?/S-001' is not a valid branch name
'--upload-pack=touch{name}' -> Fail: ... fatal: '--upload-pack=touchS-001' is not a valid branch name

cases.title: A leading dash reaches git as the name, not as an option
cases.then: git reports the candidate itself as not a valid branch name and prints no usage text.
cases.expected: Fail naming the candidate; no usage text.
cases.actual: Fail naming the candidate for all six; no usage text.

cases.title: A NUL in the format raises Fail, not ValueError
cases.given: The nul corpus family put after sdlc/{name}, plus sdlc/{name}\x00, \x00{name} and a\x00b/{name}.
cases.when: validate_format runs on each through pycall (argv cannot carry a NUL).
cases.actual: Fail: cannot check the branch format ... with git check-ref-format: embedded null byte.
cases.specSource: R-017 quote: raises Fail unless the sample passes git check-ref-format

cases.title: Shell metacharacters reach git as one argv item and run no shell
cases.given: Six no-space shell payloads such as $(>pwned){name}, `>pwned`{name}, x;>pwned;{name}, plus the injection corpus put before /{name}.
cases.when: branches.py name --format <payload> runs in a scratch repo from a watched scratch cwd.
cases.then: No pwned file appears, the tree and refs do not change, stdout is one JSON object, and ok matches the structural checks plus a direct git verdict.
cases.expected: No side effect; verdict equals the oracle.
cases.actual: No pwned file; tree unchanged; every verdict equals the oracle. $(>pwned){name} is accepted and echoed unchanged, because git accepts the name.
cases.specSource: R-017 quote; plan: the git call uses an argument list, never a shell

evidence.title: tree and refs snapshot
evidence.inline: cli-runner treeUnchanged=true for cwd and repo, every payload; no file named pwned

cases.title: A hostile cwd repo config runs no code and does not change the verdict
cases.given: The cwd is a git repo with core.fsmonitor and an alias named check-ref-format, both set to touch a PWNED file.
cases.when: branches.py name runs with sdlc/{name} and with sdlc/{name}..
cases.then: Exit 0 and exit 2, and no PWNED file in the cwd.

cases.title: A git-refused branchFormat in config.json stops every command with one JSON error
cases.given: Seven git-refused branchFormat values in .sdlc/config.json of a scratch repo with branch sdlc/S-1.
cases.when: name, parse, list and preflight --mode pr run without --format.
cases.then: Each exits 2 with one JSON object, ok false, an error with is not a valid branch name, empty stderr, and no tree or ref change.
cases.specSource: R-017 quote; spec CLI: an invalid format exits 2

cases.title: --format overrides config.json in both directions
cases.given: One repo with a valid config (feature/{name}) and one with an invalid config (-{name}).
cases.when: Each of the four commands runs with --format sdlc/{name}.. and with --format sdlc/{name} respectively.
cases.then: The invalid override exits 2; the valid override exits 0 and echoes sdlc/{name}; nothing changes on disk.

seeds.title: Invisible and terminal-control characters pass the format check
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF, U+2060, U+180E and C1 U+009B (CSI) in the literal part, because git accepts them. A branch name can then look the same as another name or carry a terminal escape. The spec delegates this to git, so it is not a defect.

seeds.title: Formats that start with refs/heads/, HEAD or @ pass
seeds.detail: refs/heads/{name}, refs/{name}, HEAD{name} and @{name} pass git check-ref-format --branch. refs/heads/{name} gives the branch refs/heads/refs/heads/S-001, which is ambiguous with refs. Consider a rule if the spec wants one.

seeds.title: A lone surrogate in a Python-side format passes
seeds.detail: validate_format('a\udc80/{name}') returns the format. Python passes the surrogate to git as byte 0x80, which git accepts. The format is not valid Unicode, so later JSON or forge calls can treat it differently.
